review_evidence: Reviewed the 432-file pinned snapshot and Sal project overview plus representative conditioned-MRDT development files.

Sal is a Lean framework and formal development for CRDT/MRDT verification, with hundreds of verification conditions, direct RA-linearizability theorems, metatheory, countermodels, and datatype-specific correctness results.
Development/probe/SPOT files can carry formal theorems and countermodels; no source-local class was proven losslessly removable.
summary: Retain Sal in full as a large formal verification and replicated-data-type metatheory corpus.

summary: Surveyed all 122 listed files (all Lean, all under Sal/MRDTs: Framework, GC, Instances, Instances/RGAKernel, Metatheory, Metatheory/Join, Metatheory/Countermodels; 994 to 129215 bytes). No build config, scripts, generated files, or non-Lean files are in the unit; lakefile.toml, lake-manifest.json and the Markdown/JSON top-level files are not listed. A line-anchored grep for theorem/lemma/def/structure/class/instance/inductive/abbrev/example/axiom/opaque finds 3918 declaration lines across the 122 files; 120 files have at least one. The two zero-declaration files, Metatheory/NegativeLedger.lean and Metatheory/PaperLedger.lean, were read completely: they are build-gate ledgers of #check commands with namespace and module-doc comments, so under FILTER-007 they are outside the pure-import class, and they carry curated theorem-name navigation (countermodels, LWW, Queue, GC, AegisSheet, RGA, Peritext results) with no verified auxiliary channel. Every file stays searchable; no exclusions.
